name: Xian Y-20 strategic airlifter
overview_md:
The Xian Y-20 ("Kunpeng") is China's strategic airlifter — the heavy transport that gives the People's Liberation Army the ability to move armour, troops and supplies across continental distances, and the platform that underpins China's growing capacity to project power far from its borders. First flown in 2013 and in service from 2016, it ended China's reliance on a handful of imported Russian Il-76s for true strategic lift.

With a maximum payload of roughly 66 tonnes, the Y-20 can carry main battle tanks and outsized cargo, and its large fleet is expanding rapidly. Early aircraft used Russian D-30 engines, but re-engining with the domestic WS-20 high-bypass turbofan has improved range and payload and removed a foreign dependency. Crucially, the airframe has spawned the YY-20 aerial-refuelling tanker, which extends the range of China's fighters and bombers — a force-multiplier for operations over the Pacific.

For an analyst, the Y-20 is strategic enabling capability rather than a weapon. Airlift and aerial refuelling determine how far and how fast a military can fight; a large Y-20/YY-20 fleet lets China sustain forces on its periphery, support disaster relief and influence operations abroad, and refuel the J-20s and H-6s that hold the Western Pacific at risk. It is, quietly, one of the more strategically consequential aircraft China has fielded.

additional.role: Strategic airlift; YY-20 aerial-refuelling tanker variant

combat_history.event: Used for COVID-era logistics, disaster relief and overseas deliveries, and increasingly for military lift exercises.
combat_history.significance: Demonstrated growing strategic-lift and influence-projection capacity.

modernization.description: Domestic high-bypass engines and a growing tanker fleet.
modernization.impact: Improves range/payload and extends the reach of PLA combat aircraft.

vulnerabilities.description: A large transport with no defences against air threats.
vulnerabilities.mitigation: Operated in secure airspace under escort.

vulnerabilities.description: Domestic WS-20 production must scale to match airframe output.
vulnerabilities.context: Engine supply has historically constrained Chinese aircraft.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Strategic airlift of forces and materiel; aerial refuelling of fighters and bombers (YY-20).
operational_patterns.typical_task_group: Supports rapid deployment and extends combat-aircraft range.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: The C-17 is the Western strategic-airlift benchmark; the Y-20 is China's broadly comparable equivalent.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: China's C-17 — how the Y-20 compares.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: China relied on imported Il-76s before the Y-20; the Y-20 is larger and more capable.
The YY-20 tanker variant parallels Western tankers in extending air reach.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: The tankers that decide how far air forces can fight.

doctrine.role: Strategic airlifter (and aerial-refuelling tanker) enabling PLA power projection and combat reach.
doctrine.employment: Moves armour and supplies over continental distances; the YY-20 refuels fighters and bombers.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Indigenous heavy lift to end reliance on imported transports and extend air reach.
doctrine.threat_context: Underpins China's ability to sustain forces on its periphery and refuel aircraft over the Pacific.
doctrine.comparison_frame: Read against the C-17, the Il-76 it replaced and Western tankers.
